parameters: There's a list of notes on recent activities in the dungeon.  One catches your eye:
"Move the farmer's little boy out of his cell and into torture at the end of the hall.  Give him a good hour before breaking him.
I normally wouldn't, but I don't question the Duke, and he doesn't care that the kid's only 13 years old.  Just do what you're told.
As usual, salt his wounds, just like you would any other torture subject, exactly as ordered."
"The Duke wants to mail the farmer a few parts of his boy to send a message.  Make sure you grind enough salt into the kid's bleeding
stumps after cutting them off.  You know how the Duke wants that sort of thing.  In fact, his orders call for extra salt for the boy's
wounds.  Again, everyone just follow instructions, and don't question any of them.  That's an order."
You find the reader accepts your key card that you found in the front barracks area.
You don't have a key card for these elevators.
You find the reader accepts your key card that you found in the front barracks area.
You don't have a key card for these elevators.
You see a young boy, perhaps 12 or 13 years old, with orange hair that looks like the farmer who asked you to find his son.  The
child is at a desk with a box full of colored pencils, a book with blank paper that he's been drawing pictures in, and an hourglass
on a table.  The hourglass looks like one of those one-hour models at a quick glance, and looks like less than 20 minutes has passed
since it was flipped, and certainly has more than half to go.
The boy is quietly crying, sobbing, as he draws in the book, occasionally stopping to look at his hands and fingers.  He looks
wired, extremely traumatized from whatever he's been through because of the Duke's men.  You feel very sorry for the boy, as you
can tell that they've been very hard on him, and he seems a bit messed up now.  He occasionally makes broken humming noises from
his throat as he draws, as if humming a tune, but he's been messed with pretty badly.
You don't see any signs of wounds or injury on his face, although his head has a spot on the back where his hair is short, where it looks
like he has some kind of bleeding injury, and although it isn't bleeding right now he has blood in his hair on the back of his head.
He is fully clothed, and some dried blood looks like it dripped out of his left-hand sleeve and onto his left hand.
You can only imagine what other injuries he has underneath his clothing and his jacket.
This makes you mad.  You have a heart for kids, for children, and this makes you angry at the Duke and his men.  You feel for this
poor kid and you want blood for what the Duke and his men have probably done to him.
The sand in the hourglass still trickling away, the child suddenly notices you and your friends enter the room and approach him.  He reacts
in a way like being startled, but also numb from being traumatized so badly.
A horrified look on his face, he slowly shakes his head side to side and recoils away from you, scared and numb.
"No...  No...  That man said I would have an hour before you come and cut off all my fingers and I don't have them
He breaks down and begins, crying, sobbing loudly, tears streaming down his face.
"Whoah!  Shhhhh...  Shhhhh...  Easy there, big guy...  You poor kid...  We're not going to hurt you...  We're not those people, and we're
not going to hurt you or your fingers...  Easy...  You're the farmer's son, right?  Your dad has a farm, and you live in some grasslands close
to the water, east of the mountains, right?  Right?"
You notice that after going through the entire dungeon area, he's the only child you've seen, anyways.
Still crying, the terrified and traumatized boy begins to shake his head up and down at your question.
"Okay, well we're here to get you out of this place and take you home, and get you away from these nasty people and this place.  Easy..."
\P[2] leans forward and tries to calm the child down, talking in a very gentle and reassuring way.
"You can trust us.  We're not with these mean people who have been bad to you.  We're not with them or the Duke at all."
Messing things up a little, \P[4] chimes in.
"Yeah we actually fight the Duke's men and kick their butt when we see them.  We're not friends with them at all, kid."
"Well you're gonna be okay now, big guy, we're here to get you home.  Easy...  That's right...
I'm \P[1], and [you point with your hand] this is \P[2], and these other guys are my friends too.  Can you tell us your name?"
In a tiny, weak voice, the still-crying boy replies.  "Jim."
His crying softens up a bit.  His spirit seems weak, but there is some hope in his eyes now as he looks at you a little
differently, as if reaching desperately for a way out of something, but weakened, numb, and badly broken.
"Okay Jim, are you ready to go?  Do you want to grab that book, or those colored pencils, or anything else?  We're gonna go home!
We're ready as soon as you are!"
Jim shakes his head.  "It's their stuff.  I don't wanna have any stuff from this place...  I wanna go home..."
"All right then Jim, let's go.  We might be able to spare a weapon or two for you.  I'm not gonna lie to you Jim, we have to fight
our way back out, like we did getting in here.  Can you fight?  Did your dad teach you to use any weapons or combat magic?"
Jim cries even a little less now, then somehow makes himself stop crying altogether.
"I can fight...  I can use a sword or an axe, and some other stuff...  As long as it isn't too big."
(Note that Jim is wounded.  His captors have, however, been feeding him.)
"We'll see about healing those wounds you have.  They didn't already cut anything off did they Jim?  You're not missing any parts?"
Jim shakes his head side to side.
"No...  But they were gonna...  They said..."
"Easy...  Shhhhh...  Shhhhh...  It's okay Jim, we're not gonna let them do that...  Now let's get you home, back to your dad, okay?"
Jim takes a moment, then tries to stop crying, and stops crying after trying a second try.
He then nods his head up and down excitedly, and brightens up a little.  He does, however, look like he's still in pain
"Hopefully this is where that poor child is being held."
"Hey did anyone catch the kid's name?  I don't remember what his name is from when we talked to the farmer."
"Wait - What's the farmer's name, by the way?"
"Geez!  I can't believe we were all so stupid!  And at the same time!  Oh this resuce is really gonna be-
-Well, we're already here, and we'll make it work anyways."
"Well I remember that he's 13 years old.  And I'm not sure what he looks like, but his father has orange hair."
